events.description: * WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet in the surf zone. * WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa Coastal Counties. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday night. For the High Surf Advisory, until midnight CST Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal; Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 12:11PM CST until November 22 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7
feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, until midnight CST Thursday
night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 1:19AM EST until November 21 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 1:30AM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10
feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

dangerous surf conditions.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current. * WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo * WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 4:26PM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
weather.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 12 feet in the surf zone. * WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 12:58AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 12 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf arrive during high tide periods. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas in and around Humboldt Bay. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday, 11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated surf. Elevated to high surf will likely continue into much of next week. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.Impacts highest across west-facing beaches, including from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday. .

For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 AM EST Sunday.

deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current. * WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo * WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 9:59PM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
weather.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 3.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties. * WHEN...From 4 AM Saturday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... North Fork Black Creek At Middleburg affecting Clay County. Additional information is available at https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX The next statement will be issued Saturday evening at 845 PM EST. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...North Fork Black Creek at Middleburg. * WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Saturday night. * IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Water begins to flood wooded areas along portions of North Fork Black Creek downstream from the gage to near Blanding Blvd. At 15.0 feet, Water begins to enter backyards of residential properties along Hawk Haven Road and Lazy Acres Road and Redbug Alley on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding begins at Enchanted Lane on the south bank of the North Fork. At 16.0 feet, Flooding expands into the yards of more properties along Lazy Acres Road on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding begins further downstream of the Blanding Blvd Bridge along North and South Lee. Flooding begins on areas of the south bank of the North Fork, particularly at Scenic Drive and Enchanted Lane. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:00 PM EST Friday the stage was 3.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.0 feet tomorrow evening. - Flood stage is 15.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Life-threatening rip current. * WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo * WHEN...Through this afternoon * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 4:10AM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through this afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
weather.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 21 at 1:30AM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 8. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 AM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected. * WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the warned area. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has issued a Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert on Saturday for the Susquehanna Valley. A Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert means that air pollution concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive groups. Sensitive groups include children, people suffering from asthma, heart disease or other lung diseases, and the elderly. The effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding strenuous activity or exercise outdoors. For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles, visit www.airnow.gov, and www.aqpartners.state.pa.us.

weather.description:

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint

Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

weather.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM EST THIS MORNING...AND AGAIN FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY. A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure. Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as much as possible. For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at: http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

* Special Marine Warning for...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm...

* Until 330 PM EST.

* At 233 PM EST, severe thunderstorms capable of producing

immediately.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises through Major Flood Stage are forecast through the middle of next week. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are inaccessible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 1:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 4.1 feet. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 2:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through the middle of next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.description:

currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 AM EST Monday.

will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach

from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 10:07AM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely
continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast
and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and
Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional
products will likely be needed into Friday.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected. * WHERE...Canovanas, Carolina, Loiza, Rio Grande... * WHEN...Until 415 PM AST. * IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Water over roadways. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 114 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. - Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 9:27AM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo.

* WHEN...Through 6 PM AST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
